1.explanation:
1. packages/react/src/components/Button/Button.js defines Button.propTypes.kind with a oneOf([...]) list that omits the string 'danger-ghost', so any use of kind="danger-ghost" triggers a warning. You need to add 'danger-ghost' to that array.

2. packages/react/src/components/Button/Button.mdx shows examples of <Button kind="danger-ghost"/>, so the docs and prop-type list are out of sync. Updating the MDX (or simply keeping the example and PropTypes in sync) will eliminate the warning and restore consistency between docs and implementation.
1.bug_scenario:
When you render the Danger Ghost Button story (i.e. <Button kind="danger-ghost">) under Storybook in dev mode, you get this warning:

  Warning: Failed prop type: Invalid prop `kind` of value `danger-ghost` supplied to `Button`, expected one of ["primary","secondary","danger","ghost","danger--primary","danger--tertiary","danger-tertiary","tertiary"].

Even though the MDX docs and the story itself both show and use “danger-ghost,” the Button component’s PropTypes list doesn’t include it, so React spits out a prop-type warning.

2.explanation: The root cause is that Button.js defines its `kind` PropTypes.oneOf list without the “danger-ghost” option, so passing kind="danger-ghost" fails validation and triggers the warning. Button.js is where the prop types and class-name mapping for each variant live and must be updated to include “danger-ghost”. In addition, Button-test.js should be updated to cover the new variant so existing tests don’t break and to verify that using kind="danger-ghost" no longer emits a warning.
2.bug_scenario: When running Storybook in development mode on the React Button component, any story that renders a “danger-ghost” button emits a prop-type warning. The warning shows that the `kind` propType for Button does not include “danger-ghost” among its allowed values, even though the docs and stories are already using that variant.
